newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany plans to rebuild strategic grain reserve.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans to rebuild strategic grain reserve.

text.p: The German farm ministry has applied for government funds to start building up emergency grain reserves over the next 10 years, a ministry official said in response to an enquiry on Thursday.
"Some 800,000 tonnes of bread wheat and rye and 190,000 tonnes of oats have been targeted," he said.
"But the process will be slow because of tight budgets and high grain prices, perhaps 70,000-80,000 tonnes a year."
The figures could vary depending on market and budget developments.
If the plan was approved, first purchases might be made in the first half of 1997.
Priority would be given to stores near milling facilities and in densely populated areas.
A ministry official told traders in Hamburg last month the reserve was necessary because public intervention stocks had fallen amid farm reform efforts and buoyant world demand.
Germany last had less than one million tonnes of grain left in its public stores, compared with four million tonnes a year ago.
"That grain technically belongs to Brussels so it could be shipped to southern Europe if there was a drought," the Bonn offical said.
"A national reserve is legally mandatory to provide for such unforeseen events as the Chernobyl nuclear accident 10 years ago."
